nodes.name: Liquid phase reduction of CoCrOx
nodes.procedure: Dissolve 11.90 g of CoCl₂·6H₂O and 13.32 g of CrCl₃·6H₂O in 25 mL of deionized (DI) water to make a 2 M metal chloride solution and set aside. Take 2 mL of the above prepared CoCl₂ and CrCl₃ solutions respectively and mix them evenly. Prepare a fresh solution of sodium borohydride by dissolving 3 g of NaBH₄ in 20 mL of DI water, then add dropwise to the above mixture of metal ion chlorides, stir mechanically for 15 min, allow to cool, then leave overnight and freeze dry. After freeze-drying, the catalyst was repeatedly washed using DI water and ethanol, and dried under vacuum to obtain the CoCrOx catalyst.

nodes.source_text: The OER activity measurements of the catalysts were conducted in O2-saturated 1 M KOH solution by using a standard three-electrode system... CoCrOx exhibited superior OER performance, necessitating a mere overpotential of 268 mV to achieve the current density of 10 mA cm−2... at 400 mV_i, the current density of CoCrOx considerably exceeded other catalysts, being 10.7 times, 3.4 times, and twice as high as FeCrOx, NiCrOx, and RuO2... Tafel slope of 101.6 mV dec−1... R_ct (9.0 Ω)... C_dl for CoCrOx was calculated to be 16.45 mF cm−2

nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the prepared catalysts was observed using the scanning electron microscopy (SEM), revealing the porous characteristics of FeCrOx, CoCrOx and NiCrOx (Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows no obvious lattice striations for CoCrOx, indicating amorphous nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) and aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC HAADF-STEM) further showed that there were no obvious lattice striations (Fig. 2e and Supplementary Fig. 2), indicating its amorphous nature.

properties.description: High-resolution image showing lattice fringes and nanoparticle morphology with crystalline domains

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows very broad and weak diffraction peaks, indicating long-range disorder feature of the catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern (Supplementary Fig. 3) showed very broad and weak diffraction peaks, indicating the long-range disorder feature.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows diffraction rings confirming amorphous character with bright inner rings suggesting short-range order.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amorphous character is further confirmed by the diffraction rings shown by selected area electron diffraction (SAED) (Fig. 2f), with the bright inner rings suggesting the short-range order feature.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows Co, Cr, and O uniformly distributed throughout CoCrOx architecture, demonstrating formation of CoCr oxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping analysis showed that Co, Cr, and O were uniformly distributed throughout the architecture (Fig. 2g), demonstrating the formation of CoCr oxides rather than phase-separated mixed structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES shows atomic ratios of Fe, Co, Ni to Cr close to 1:1 for the prepared catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometer (ICP-AES) was used to further determine the elemental ratios of the prepared catalysts (Supplementary Table 1). The results showed that the atomic ratios of Fe, Co, Ni to Cr were close to 1:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS confirms CoCrOx, FeCrOx and NiCrOx catalysts have similar local structures and coordination environments.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra was used to confirm that the CoCrOx, FeCrOx and NiCrOx (Fig. 2h, i and Supplementary Figs. 9–12) catalysts had similar local structures and coordination environments.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows CoCrOx located between CoO and Co3O4; Cr K-edge shows Cr valence state +3 for all catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By X-ray near-edge structural absorption spectroscopy (XANES), we were able to precisely determine the valence states of the active elements. ... Figure 4b shows that the Cr K-edge of all catalysts almost overlaps with Cr2O3, pointing to the valence state of Cr is +3.

nodes.characterization_summary: sXAS confirms Cr doping decreases average valence state of Co in CoCrOx; shows conspicuous valence change in Co during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the leftward shift of the absorption edge of CoCrOx relative to CoOx indicates that the Cr doping decreases the average valence state of Co, which matches the stronger lower valence absorption peak in the soft XAS (sXAS) (Supplementary Fig. 20).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms coexistence of +2 and +3 valences for active metal elements and Cr +3 valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The coexistence of both +2 and +3 valences for each active metal element in X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) also confirms the above conclusion (Supplementary Fig. 21a–f and Supplementary Table 3).
